newsitem.title: JAPAN: Green Cross says expects net losses in 96/97,97/98.
newsitem.headline: Green Cross says expects net losses in 96/97,97/98.

text.p: Green Cross Corp said on Wednesday that it expects to post a parent net loss in the current business year to March 31, 1997, and the following year due to compensation payments to victims who used its blood products that were tainted by the HIV virus that causes AIDS.
A Green Cross spokesman did not give specific figures for the expected net losses.
Green Cross said in May that it expected a parent current profit of three billion yen in 1996/97, but it did not give a forecast for net earnings at that time.
Green Cross expects to change its president in early September and it will announce a new management plan at the same time, the company spokesman said.
The Japanese drug firm has been accused of spreading the HIV infection through the sale of unheated blood products in a decade-old medical scandal which has claimed about 400 lives.
Green Cross is facing civil lawsuits over the scandal. It has settled 27 cases and has paid a total of 5.8 billion yen in compensation to the victims since April 1, the spokesman said.
Another 42 cases are still pending, he said.
